Colombia.name: Bogotá
Colombia.note: High-altitude capital on the Bogotá savanna (2,640 m); Andean political and financial centre.

Colombia.name: Medellín
Colombia.note: Antioquia's capital, in the Aburrá valley; a former cartel stronghold now a services/innovation hub.

Colombia.name: Cartagena
Colombia.note: Walled Caribbean port city, UNESCO World Heritage — colonial Spanish fortifications.

Venezuela.name: Caracas
Venezuela.note: Capital in a narrow valley near the Caribbean coast; seat of PDVSA, the state oil company.

Venezuela.name: Maracaibo
Venezuela.note: On Lake Maracaibo; heart of Venezuela's oil-producing region.

Guyana.name: Georgetown
Guyana.note: Low-lying coastal capital, protected by a seawall; only English-speaking country in South America.

Suriname.name: Paramaribo
Suriname.note: Former Dutch colonial capital on the Suriname River; UNESCO-listed inner city.

Ecuador.name: Quito
Ecuador.note: High-Andean capital near the equator; second-highest official capital city in the world.

Ecuador.name: Guayaquil
Ecuador.note: Largest city and main Pacific port; export hub for bananas and shrimp.

Peru.name: Lima
Peru.note: Coastal desert capital founded by Pizarro in 1535; over a third of Peru's population; hosted the COP20 UN climate conference in 2014; Peru's coastal desert has historically been rich in phosphate/nitrate (guano) deposits

Peru.name: Cusco
Peru.note: Former Inca capital; gateway to Machu Picchu, in the Sacred Valley.

Peru.name: Iquitos
Peru.note: Largest city in the world unreachable by road — only by river or air, deep in the Amazon.

Brazil.name: Brasília
Brazil.note: Purpose-built capital (1960), modernist plan by Niemeyer/Costa; replaced Rio as capital; of Brazil's 10 South American neighbours, only Ecuador and Chile don't share a border with it

Brazil.name: Rio de Janeiro
Brazil.note: Former capital; Sugarloaf, Christ the Redeemer, and the country's cultural face abroad; Copacabana Beach is its best-known stretch of coastline

Brazil.name: São Paulo
Brazil.note: Largest city in South America; Brazil's financial and industrial core; its Fazenda coffee-growing hinterland exports through the port of Santos

Brazil.name: Manaus
Brazil.note: Amazon rainforest hub at the Rio Negro–Solimões confluence (the 'meeting of waters').

Brazil.name: Santos
Brazil.note: Brazil's busiest port, on the coast near São Paulo — main export outlet for the Fazenda coffee region.

Brazil.name: Carajás
Brazil.note: Site of the Carajás mining complex — one of the world's largest iron-ore deposits, in Pará state.

Bolivia.name: Sucre
Bolivia.note: Constitutional capital and seat of the judiciary — Bolivia has two capitals; Bolivia is one of only two landlocked countries in South America, along with Paraguay

Bolivia.name: La Paz
Bolivia.note: Administrative/executive seat of government; highest capital in the world (~3,650 m); Bolivia is one of only two landlocked countries in South America, along with Paraguay

Bolivia.name: Santa Cruz
Bolivia.note: Largest city; lowland economic engine, distinct from the Andean highlands politically.

Chile.name: Santiago
Chile.note: Capital in the Central Valley between the Andes and the Coast Range; Chile's territory also includes Easter Island (Rapa Nui), far out in the Pacific

Chile.name: Valparaíso
Chile.note: Chile's National Congress sits here, not Santiago; major Pacific port.

Chile.name: Antofagasta
Chile.note: Copper-mining port on the edge of the Atacama Desert.

Chile.name: Arica
Chile.note: Chile's northernmost city, in the Atacama — one of the driest inhabited places on Earth.

Chile.name: Chuquicamata
Chile.note: Site of one of the world's largest open-pit copper mines, near Calama.

Paraguay.name: Asunción
Paraguay.note: On the Paraguay River; one of the oldest cities in South America (founded 1537); Paraguay is one of only two landlocked countries in South America, along with Bolivia

Argentina.name: Buenos Aires
Argentina.note: Río de la Plata capital; the country's primate city by a wide margin; the UK's nearby Falkland Islands (Islas Malvinas) remain a live territorial dispute, and the cause of the 1982 Falklands War

Argentina.name: Córdoba
Argentina.note: Second city; industrial and university centre in the Pampas' northwest.

Argentina.name: Ushuaia
Argentina.note: World's southernmost city of its size — gateway to Antarctica and Tierra del Fuego; Cape Horn and the Drake Passage — the stormy gap to Antarctica — lie just south

Uruguay.name: Montevideo
Uruguay.note: Capital on the Río de la Plata estuary; home to most of Uruguay's population.

French Guiana.name: Cayenne
French Guiana.note: Prefecture of this French overseas department — part of the European Union and eurozone, in South America.

French Guiana.name: Kourou
French Guiana.note: Home to the Guiana Space Centre (CNES/ESA/Arianespace) — its near-equatorial latitude (~5°N) gives rockets an extra boost from Earth's spin.

Canada.name: Ottawa
Canada.note: Chosen by Queen Victoria (1857) partly for its inland, defensible position between Toronto and Montreal.

Canada.name: Toronto
Canada.note: Largest city; Ontario's capital and Canada's financial hub, on Lake Ontario.

Canada.name: Vancouver
Canada.note: Pacific port city, gateway to Asia trade; consistently ranked among the most livable cities.

United States.name: Washington, D.C.
United States.note: Federal capital carved as its own district (not a state) so no state would hold outsized power.

United States.name: New York City
United States.note: Largest US city; UN headquarters, global financial centre (Wall Street).

United States.name: Los Angeles
United States.note: Pacific coast hub; entertainment industry (Hollywood) and major container port.

United States.name: Chicago
United States.note: Great Lakes hub on Lake Michigan; historic railroad and commodities-trading centre.

Mexico.name: Mexico City
Mexico.note: Built over the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan on a drained lakebed — sinking slowly as a result.

Mexico.name: Guadalajara
Mexico.note: Birthplace of mariachi and tequila culture; second-largest metro area.

Mexico.name: Cancún
Mexico.note: Caribbean resort city on the Yucatán Peninsula, near Maya ruins.

Guatemala.name: Guatemala City
Guatemala.note: Highland capital; most populous city in Central America.

Honduras.name: Tegucigalpa
Honduras.note: Mountain-basin capital named for a nearby silver-mining hill.

Nicaragua.name: Managua
Nicaragua.note: On the shore of Lake Managua, in an active seismic/volcanic zone.

Costa Rica.name: San José
Costa Rica.note: Central Valley capital; Costa Rica abolished its army in 1948, unusual in the region.

Panama.name: Panama City
Panama.note: At the Pacific mouth of the Panama Canal, the key interoceanic shipping shortcut.

Cuba.name: Havana
Cuba.note: Caribbean's largest city; colonial Old Havana is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Jamaica.name: Kingston
Jamaica.note: Natural harbour capital; birthplace of reggae music.

Haiti.name: Port-au-Prince
Haiti.note: Capital of the world's first Black republic (independence 1804).

Dominican Republic.name: Santo Domingo
Dominican Republic.note: Oldest continuously inhabited European-founded city in the Americas (1496).

Morocco.name: Rabat
Morocco.note: Atlantic coast capital; administrative centre, distinct from the larger Casablanca.

Morocco.name: Casablanca
Morocco.note: Morocco's largest city and main port; economic capital.

Algeria.name: Algiers
Algeria.note: Mediterranean capital of Africa's largest country by area.

Libya.name: Tripoli
Libya.note: Mediterranean coastal capital; major Sahara oil-export economy.

Egypt.name: Cairo
Egypt.note: Africa's largest city, on the Nile near the Giza pyramids.

Egypt.name: Alexandria
Egypt.note: Ancient Mediterranean port founded by Alexander the Great; famous ancient library.

Mauritania.name: Nouakchott
Mauritania.note: Sahara-edge Atlantic capital, expanded rapidly after independence (1960).

Mali.name: Bamako
Mali.note: On the Niger River; gateway to historic Timbuktu further north.

Niger.name: Niamey
Niger.note: On the Niger River, on the southern edge of the Sahara.

Chad.name: N'Djamena
Chad.note: At the Chari–Logone confluence, near Lake Chad and the Cameroon border.

Sudan.name: Khartoum
Sudan.note: At the confluence of the Blue Nile and White Nile — the true start of the Nile.

Nigeria.name: Abuja
Nigeria.note: Purpose-built central capital (1991), replacing Lagos to sit neutrally between regions.

Nigeria.name: Lagos
Nigeria.note: Former capital; Africa's largest city and Nigeria's commercial/port hub.

Ethiopia.name: Addis Ababa
Ethiopia.note: One of Africa's highest capitals (~2,355 m); seat of the African Union.

Kenya.name: Nairobi
Kenya.note: East African hub; Nairobi National Park sits inside the city limits.

DR Congo.name: Kinshasa
DR Congo.note: On the Congo River, facing Brazzaville (Republic of Congo) across the water.

Angola.name: Luanda
Angola.note: Atlantic port capital; oil exports drive the economy.

South Africa.name: Pretoria
South Africa.note: Administrative capital — one of three, alongside Cape Town (legislative) and Bloemfontein (judicial).

South Africa.name: Cape Town
South Africa.note: Legislative capital, beneath Table Mountain, near the Cape of Good Hope.

South Africa.name: Johannesburg
South Africa.note: Not a capital, but the largest city — grew around 1880s gold-mining on the Witwatersrand.

Madagascar.name: Antananarivo
Madagascar.note: Highland capital of the world's fourth-largest island, known for endemic species.

United Kingdom.name: London
United Kingdom.note: On the Thames; former hub of the British Empire, global financial centre.

Ireland.name: Dublin
Ireland.note: On the River Liffey; European tech-sector hub for many multinational HQs.

France.name: Paris
France.note: On the Seine; seat of the EU alongside Brussels/Strasbourg in influence, not formally.

Spain.name: Madrid
Spain.note: Geographic and highest-altitude capital in Western Europe, on the Meseta Central.

Spain.name: Barcelona
Spain.note: Catalonia's capital; major Mediterranean port with a strong regional identity.

Portugal.name: Lisbon
Portugal.note: Atlantic-facing capital; launch point for the Age of Discovery voyages.

Germany.name: Berlin
Germany.note: Reunified in 1990 after Cold War division; the Wall's line still traces through the city.

Germany.name: Frankfurt
Germany.note: Financial capital — seat of the European Central Bank.

Italy.name: Rome
Italy.note: Encircles Vatican City, an independent state within the city.

Italy.name: Milan
Italy.note: Italy's financial and fashion capital, in the industrial Po Valley.

Switzerland.name: Bern
Switzerland.note: De facto capital ('federal city'); Switzerland has no constitutionally declared capital.

Netherlands.name: Amsterdam
Netherlands.note: Constitutional capital; the seat of government is actually The Hague.

Poland.name: Warsaw
Poland.note: Rebuilt almost entirely after near-total WWII destruction; Old Town is UNESCO-listed.

Ukraine.name: Kyiv
Ukraine.note: On the Dnieper River; one of the oldest cities in Eastern Europe (Kyivan Rus').

Romania.name: Bucharest
Romania.note: Once nicknamed 'Little Paris' for its early-20th-century Belle Époque architecture.

Greece.name: Athens
Greece.note: Cradle of Western democracy and philosophy; the Acropolis overlooks the city.

Sweden.name: Stockholm
Sweden.note: Built across 14 islands on Lake Mälaren where it meets the Baltic Sea.

Norway.name: Oslo
Norway.note: At the head of the Oslofjord; hosts the Nobel Peace Prize ceremony each year.

Russia (European).name: Moscow
Russia (European).note: European Russia's core — the country's landmass extends across Siberia deep into Asia.

Russia (European).name: St. Petersburg
Russia (European).note: Former imperial capital, built by Peter the Great on the Neva delta as a 'window to Europe'.

Turkey.name: Ankara
Turkey.note: Interior Anatolian capital, chosen over Istanbul after the republic's founding (1923).

Turkey.name: Istanbul
Turkey.note: Straddles Europe and Asia across the Bosphorus; former Byzantine/Ottoman capital.

Saudi Arabia.name: Riyadh
Saudi Arabia.note: Interior Najd-plateau capital, seat of the ruling Al Saud dynasty.

Saudi Arabia.name: Mecca
Saudi Arabia.note: Islam's holiest city and the Hajj pilgrimage site — birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad.

Iraq.name: Baghdad
Iraq.note: On the Tigris; former seat of the medieval Abbasid Caliphate's House of Wisdom.

Iran.name: Tehran
Iran.note: At the foot of the Alborz mountains; became capital under the Qajar dynasty (1795).

Afghanistan.name: Kabul
Afghanistan.note: High-altitude capital (~1,790 m) in a valley on the historic Silk Road route.

Kazakhstan.name: Astana
Kazakhstan.note: Purpose-planned capital since 1997, replacing Almaty; renamed several times since.

Mongolia.name: Ulaanbaatar
Mongolia.note: World's coldest capital city; historically a centre of nomadic pastoral trade.

China.name: Beijing
China.note: Capital for most of the last 800 years; home to the Forbidden City.

China.name: Shanghai
China.note: Largest city; China's financial and shipping hub on the Yangtze delta.

China.name: Xi'an
China.note: Ancient imperial capital; eastern terminus of the Silk Road, home to the Terracotta Army.

Japan.name: Tokyo
Japan.note: World's most populous metropolitan area; capital since 1868 (formerly Edo).

North Korea.name: Pyongyang
North Korea.note: On the Taedong River; rebuilt as a showcase capital after Korean War destruction.

South Korea.name: Seoul
South Korea.note: On the Han River; one of the world's leading tech and manufacturing hubs.

Nepal.name: Kathmandu
Nepal.note: Himalayan valley capital; gateway to Everest expeditions.

India.name: New Delhi
India.note: Planned capital (1911) beside old Delhi; seat of Parliament and the Rashtrapati Bhavan.

India.name: Mumbai
India.note: Financial capital, on a natural harbour; home to the Bombay Stock Exchange.

India.name: Chennai
India.note: Major Bay of Bengal port and automotive manufacturing hub.

Pakistan.name: Islamabad
Pakistan.note: Planned capital (1960s) built near Rawalpindi, at the foot of the Margalla Hills.

Pakistan.name: Karachi
Pakistan.note: Former capital; Pakistan's largest city and main Arabian Sea port.

Bangladesh.name: Dhaka
Bangladesh.note: One of the world's most densely populated cities, on the Buriganga River.

Sri Lanka.name: Colombo
Sri Lanka.note: Commercial capital and main port; the official capital is Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte nearby.

Myanmar.name: Naypyidaw
Myanmar.note: Purpose-built capital since 2005, replacing Yangon; sparsely populated by design.

Thailand.name: Bangkok
Thailand.note: On the Chao Phraya delta; one of the world's most-visited cities.

Vietnam.name: Hanoi
Vietnam.note: Red River Delta capital with over a thousand years as Vietnam's political centre.

Vietnam.name: Ho Chi Minh City
Vietnam.note: Formerly Saigon; Vietnam's largest city and economic engine in the Mekong Delta region.

Indonesia.name: Jakarta
Indonesia.note: Current seat of government on Java — sinking fast, prompting the move to Nusantara.

Indonesia.name: Nusantara
Indonesia.note: New purpose-built capital under construction on Borneo, replacing sinking, congested Jakarta.

Philippines.name: Manila
Philippines.note: On Manila Bay; one of the most densely populated cities on Earth.

Australia.name: Canberra
Australia.note: Purpose-built compromise capital (1908), roughly midway between rivals Sydney and Melbourne.

Australia.name: Sydney
Australia.note: Largest city, on a natural harbour; site of the first British penal colony (1788).

Australia.name: Melbourne
Australia.note: Cultural/sporting capital; was Australia's capital until Canberra was completed in 1927.

New Zealand.name: Wellington
New Zealand.note: World's southernmost national capital, on Cook Strait between the North and South Islands.

New Zealand.name: Auckland
New Zealand.note: Largest city, built across an active volcanic field on an isthmus between two harbours.

Papua New Guinea.name: Port Moresby
Papua New Guinea.note: Coastal capital of one of the world's most linguistically diverse countries (800+ languages).

Fiji.name: Suva
Fiji.note: On Viti Levu; regional diplomatic hub for the South Pacific.
